item.title: There’s an Ordinary Beauty to These Middle Years with Kids
item.description: “Just wait—before you know it, they’ll be all grown up!” I heard this countless times when my three children were little. It came from the stranger in the grocery store checkout line who commented on my little boy’s red hair, or the women who volunteered to keep my daughters in the church nursery. In those days, everything was full: the diaper bag, the laundry bin, my scattered brain, my hands, and my heart. item.title: The Weight of Always Being “On”
item.description: There’s a kind of exhaustion sleep can’t fix. The kind that builds quietly from being needed all the time. It’s the mental load, the emotional load, the “I just need a minute but there are no minutes left” load. It’s living in a state of permanent readiness—the human version of a smoke detector that never gets to power down. Even when I’m “off,” I’m not really off. item.title: To All the Non-Festive Moms: I See You
item.description: To all the non-festive moms out there: I see you. It’s hard to find you among a sea of holiday sweaters and jingle bells. item.description: The other night, while my 7-year-old son was brushing his teeth, he spotted a shiny candy wrapper sticking out of the bathroom trash can. His eyes widened. item.title: This Simple Life Is Beautiful
item.description: We might not have the newest electronics. Our kids might have to work to earn that electric scooter. We might not go on fancy vacations—or any vacations at all. When we do eat out, we might split an adult meal between the little ones, because eating out is a rare treat. We might pay for a movie at home instead of going to the theater. item.title: Getting through Christmas without Your Kids
item.description: When you are divorced, one of the hardest kinds of loneliness as a mother is being without your children for Christmas. It’s not uncommon for divorced couples to alternate Christmas with the kids each year, and let me tell you, no matter how often you’ve been doing this, it never gets easier. Sure, you’ll go through the motions of preparing for Christmas, like you always do. item.title: 10 Years after My Mother’s Death, Her Faith Still Guides Me
item.description: Growing up, I was a reluctant Catholic. My mother would drag us to church, and I’d go through the motions—fingers moving across rosary beads without really feeling the prayers. But she never stopped. Sunday Mass, daily prayers, devotions to the Blessed Mother. She was relentless in her faith, not because she was trying to force it on us, but because she genuinely believed we would need it someday. She was right. item.title: The Empty Chair
item.description: The holidays are fun. And hard. I always feel so blessed. And also so empty at times. Each aspect of preparing. Enjoying. Every outing. Laugh. Gift. Shared meal. Seems different.
